fatal_errors: The proposed material is a Cu-doped, nominally single-phase AlCoCrFeNi alloy rather than as-cast dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.
The response invents dopant-induced grain-boundary segregation, whereas the target transition arises intrinsically from L12 ordering and evolution of jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
It omits the critical aging conditions and observed minimum/recovery near 600°C and 750°C.
The cited evidence does not demonstrate Cu-induced temper embrittlement, grain-boundary segregation, or a ductile-brittle-ductile transition in the proposed alloy.
explanation: The hypothesis captures only the broad idea that an HEA might exhibit a non-monotonic ductility response over an intermediate thermal window. It does not reconstruct the target material, thermal intervention, microstructural mediator, or mechanism. Its single-phase starting-state assumption is also questionable for Al-containing AlCoCrFeNi alloys. The proposed control-versus-doped temperature sweep is falsifiable, but lacks a justified temperature window and sufficiently sensitive grain-boundary chemistry measurements; SEM-EDS would generally be inadequate for dilute segregation. Most importantly, E1 concerns Hf/Mo additions to a different CCA and E2 provides general phase-formation background, so neither supports the asserted Cu-segregation mechanism. The proposal is therefore a speculative alternative rather than an evidence-supported reconstruction.
